investigations.title: pkg/state: reflection CPU and allocation profiles
investigations.summary:
The recorded profiling and fixed comparisons are complete. Their mixed and negative results remain below; the subsequent decoded-frame qualification and architecture experiments continue in the separate state design investigation. This profiling record has no pending execution or contributor decision.

The completed pointer experiments remain unpromoted: the first coherent-pointer comparison had five timing regressions, two gains and twelve nonsignificant results; the enclosing-pointer comparison had three regressions, four gains and twelve nonsignificant results. Earlier helper, map-registration and reader experiments remain separate evidence.

The generated restore successor is now implemented and independently correctness-qualified. It uses one authoritative graph pointer and a static restoration callback, shared map/array ordering, typed destination operations and exact registered-type callback selection. Four corrected full suites plus eighteen retained owners and two production links pass; thirteen serialized streams match across four groups. Original shared-fixture construction failures remain recorded. Runtime-sized slice backing retains the existing reflection boundary.

Its fixed comparison is mixed and unpromoted: five Load timing gains, two adoption slowdowns and twelve nonsignificant timings across 52 actions and 456 rows. Load allocations fall, while the state and UDP test executables grow 19.54% and 25.48%. The separate RestoreEmpty pilot passes all six save/load iterations, with overlapping Load ranges and a 21.50% larger runsc; three CPUID-warmed operations per arm are descriptive, not a significance or cold-start result.

A separate two-line shared-envelope consolidation at b941f2f056 passes six owners and four matched executable checks. It reduces runsc by 1,634,304 bytes on AMD64 and 1,507,328 bytes on ARM64 relative to the measured successor. Timing was not rerun, so this size result does not remove the earlier performance limitations. A further shared-struct helper at 2831e4a8e2 passes six owners and three groups of thirteen matching streams. Its matched executables shrink again relative to b941: runsc by 1,814,528 bytes on AMD64 and 1,507,328 bytes on ARM64. The subsequent fixed shared-struct comparison is independently closed and still mixed: nine timing gains, three regressions and seven nonsignificant results. Focused captured/uncaptured adoption profiles are also closed. Array restoration occupies 42.58% and 46.08% cumulative CPU in the candidate profiles, including nested restoration, statistics and waits; those overlapping sampled totals do not identify reflection alone as the cause or predict a speedup. No successor is proposed for adoption.

The runtime-array revision at e0515a1d8b has a fully reviewed fixed comparison against coherent control 225fdf9301. It shows five Load timing gains, a 3.54% UDP Save regression (p=.039), and thirteen nonsignificant timings. Captured and uncaptured adoption Load medians rise 2.62% and 3.45%, respectively, without statistical significance; that does not establish equivalence. The state and UDP test executables grow 50.24% and 59.79%. This revision remains unpromoted.

The shared array-loop/view revision at 173993df1f passed six test/analyzer owners and three groups of thirteen matching streams. Its state and UDP test executables are 8,573,088 and 8,994,976 bytes, down 5.42% and 5.87% from e051. Its original production-link deadline is retained separately from the completed link continuation. The subsequent shared-pointer helper at fffd29842d6d passed the focused correctness checks and production links. Its runsc executables are 54,141,088 bytes on AMD64 and 50,790,560 bytes on ARM64. The AMD64 executable remains 37.23% larger than the retained coherent control (39,452,832 bytes); the production comparison has a recorded version-stamp input difference and is not a byte-attribution or startup claim.

The shared-pointer fixed comparison 8ae794ca is independently closed: seven timing gains, five regressions and seven nonsignificant results. Captured and uncaptured adoption Load regress 4.60% and 6.91%; state and UDP test executables remain 38.29% and 46.16% larger than the matched coherent control. This mixed result remains unpromoted.

The earlier shared-pointer idle-Nginx restore pilot remains independently confirmed incomplete: each arm produced two one-iteration observations, then the third restore failed during Docker/containerd checkpoint upload. The four observed rows do not complete the required six-row pilot. Native exit status, BEP and parent status incorrectly reported success despite benchmark failure text and XML failures; the original discrepancy is retained. It supplies no complete end-to-end comparison or adoption claim.

The data-plan successor at 221124de7 is independently correctness-qualified. Its fixed comparison has seven timing regressions, one gain and eleven nonsignificant results, and remains unpromoted. State/UDP test executables grow 2.64%/2.81%; matched runsc files grow 2.41% on AMD64 and 2.48% on ARM64. Reviewed diagnostic profiles identify per-Load metadata construction and recurring dispatch/parsing costs without proving causal effect sizes. A separate Nginx pilot completes three actual restores per arm; overlapping small-sample timings do not establish a performance improvement.

The metadata-ownership revision at 5401bbaba is independently qualified for the selected correctness and race checks, with three groups of thirteen streams matching the prior data-plan source. Single measured-Load allocation reductions are observed, alongside increased initialization allocation counts. The adoption fixture uses Save-only setup, but ControlMessageDecoding performs an untimed validation Load before measurement; its row is not a first-use layout cost. Each timing has only one observation, so these measurements do not establish a timing improvement. Production executable sizes are unchanged from 221124de7 and remain about 2.4% larger than the coherent control. The candidate remains unpromoted.

The fixed idle-Nginx comparison of metadata-ownership source 5401bbaba against coherent control 3aa3a761c is independently closed: all twenty-four actual checkpoint-and-restore operations completed, twelve per arm, each starting a fresh sentry. Median observed time rises from 0.876 seconds to 1.157 seconds (31.98%). The measurement includes restore and port-presence detection, not HTTP readiness or populated traffic. Repetitions share one worker per arm, so worker effects remain uncontrolled and the difference cannot be attributed solely to code. The candidate remains unpromoted.

The narrower owner-lookup revision at e444abe2e is independently closed for ten fresh correctness/analyzer owners and single measured-Load cost checks. The control-message observation uses 96 more bytes with the same 102 allocations after an untimed validation Load; it is not a first-use layout cost. Initialization totals are unchanged. Test executable file lengths are unchanged, with text sections 192 bytes larger. Single measured-load observations and the closed diagnostic profiles do not establish a latency improvement; the candidate remains experimental and unpromoted.

The byte-reader comparison is independently closed. On the deterministic synthetic pointer/slice graph through the real uncompressed statefile reader, twelve fixed balanced pairs show no detected time benefit (median 766,202.5 to 760,387 ns, p=.198), 16 additional bytes per operation and unchanged 4,953 allocations per operation. All twenty-six native processes exited successfully, with twenty-four measured rows; the original parent failure and XML reporter errors remain recorded. These saved measurements were authenticated without rerunning benchmarks. This is not a whole-kernel restore or fresh-sentry startup measurement. The byte-reader revision remains unpromoted.

The decoded-frame architecture uses one parser and generated restoration methods. Both stable-block and inline candidates remain unadopted. The simpler contiguous revision passes correctness and its fixed comparison: large synthetic Load is 19.00% faster with 36.85% fewer allocated bytes, while control-message timing has no detected change. Executable file sizes are unchanged. Independent review is complete. The completed 24-operation whole-restore comparison does not establish an overall speedup. Subsequent profiling and the unsuccessful type-description sharing experiment are recorded in the design investigation; no successor has been adopted.

findings.text: Map reflection was the strongest measured reflection opportunity. In sampled allocation-object profiles, reflect.unsafe_New accounted for 51.12% flat in Map Load and 25.41% flat in Map Save. Map Save also spent 25.13% cumulative CPU in MapKeys and 15.24% in MapIndex; cumulative entries overlap and must not be added.

Other costs would survive simply replacing reflective field access: Stats.sample accounted for 21.24% cumulative CPU in Pointer Load, while the 32-packet UDP Save profile attributed 40.06% of sampled allocation objects to wire.Struct.Alloc and 26.53% to encodeStruct. Sample percentages are estimates, not exact allocation counts or predicted savings.

All five profiling actions completed, but the original parent failed because its collector expected a ZIP. The ten individual CPU/heap files were retained and decoded in a tool-only continuation, with no benchmark repetition. The original failed parent remains failed.

Independent saved-result review verified all 192 measured rows, 12 balanced AB/BA pairs and the actual source-to-binary inputs. Map Save medians were 240.95 versus 214.75 ns per normalized unit (benchstat −10.87%, p=.020, 12 samples per side); allocated bytes were 156 versus 129 (−17.31%). None of the seven other timing comparisons was statistically significant in this run; this does not establish equivalence. The production difference is only the delivered MapRange loop.

Source review withdrew the first one-line decoder preallocation candidate before testing. Normal referenced maps are eagerly allocated in decodeObject before decodeMap, so adding a size hint only in decodeMap misses the owning allocation path. No preallocation measurements were run; the next candidate must address the actual map-creation path.

evidence.label: Decoder allocation ownership in the measured cohort

findings.text: The struct/header coallocation experiment changes only encode.go and wire.go against the fixed-work baseline. Independent review verified 264 measured rows and 12 balanced before/after pairs per cohort. Control-message Save uses 11.76% fewer allocations; UDP queue Save uses 12.83%, 19.03% and 20.30% fewer at 1, 8 and 32 packets. All eleven timing comparisons are nonsignificant (smallest p=.060). Allocated bytes are essentially unchanged and serialized sizes are identical. This remains an experiment, not a ready PR or checkpoint-speedup claim.

Reusing decoder temporary key/value slots outside Struct and Array kinds reduced the fixed 1024-entry Map Load median from 449,457 to 368,672 ns (-17.97%, benchstat p<.001, n=12). Allocated bytes fell 6.71% and allocations fell 52.47%. Root verified the original 192 measured rows and 12 pairs. Only decode.go differs between the measured inputs; the seven other timing comparisons were nonsignificant.

Reusing scalar iterator storage reduced the separate fixed 1024-entry Map Save median from 195,068 to 184,478.5 ns (-5.43%, benchstat p=.010, n=12). Allocated bytes fell 6.17% and allocations fell 35.82%; seven other timing comparisons were nonsignificant. The original measured rows and numeric interpretation are independently reviewed. MapRange #15542 subsequently landed, and the contributor-approved iterator-storage change is delivered as PR #15621.

The shared-primitive prototype at 74c23e08a passed the selected five-owner compatibility scope. In the paired study, pointer Load improved by 7.72% (p=.002); the other eight timing changes were not significant, and allocation counts did not change. Executable size still increased: UDP by 15% and state by 7.1%. CPU/heap capture and pointer-only controls have since completed. Direct generated emission is now the primary architectural experiment; this shared-primitive prototype is not an upstream-ready proposal.

evidence.label: Completed CPU and heap profile capture

findings.text: The first direct framed prototype is public at b83596347, with qualification e0292b990. It captures generated primitive fields directly and retains the existing graph, hooks and deferred reference ownership. The appended experimental format is opt-in; older readers do not support it. Correctness run 2b48aa70 passed all five runtime actions and three analyzers. Two analyzers failed on an unused initial Scalar value at framed_unsafe.go:51; the failed parent is retained. An initializer-only continuation f34a56f9 completed successfully. The subsequent paired framed measurements are complete and reported separately below.

The direct framed experiment regressed all nine timing comparisons (p<.001). At 32 queued UDP packets, Save time increased 24.98%, allocated bytes increased 69.05%, and wire bytes increased 16.76%, even though allocation count fell 41.48%. Pointer Load took 40.86% more time. Root verified these values against the original benchstat output. The process-level RSS observations do not establish an improvement. This slower prototype is not an upstream proposal; the owner subsequently completed the six-operation RestoreEmpty compatibility pilot and hotspot profiles. That pilot also had worse timing/image size and is not a statistical performance comparison. Subsequent existing-wire and direct-layout measurements also failed to establish an overall speedup; their results remain separate.

The first existing-wire direct-storage experiment preserves wire size but regresses UDP Save time by 6.69% and allocated bytes by 8.80%, despite 35.69% fewer allocations. Control-message Save/Load regress 63.85%/104.48%. The follow-up layout experiment also shows no speedup: UDP time is not significant (p=.068), allocations fall 37.21% while bytes rise 7.31%, and control Save/Load regress 14.10%/24.74%. These are separate matched 12-pair experiments; their timings are not comparisons across workers. Neither design is ready for upstream.

The independent primitive-array prototype keeps the Array wire grammar and copies captured values into owned storage. The actual addressable-versus-value fixture failed for signaling float32 NaNs before correction; complex64 matched. Corrected source cd66d9b1dd stores the float32 promotion in owned float64 values. All 11 selected targets passed, including baseline state, corrected state/wire on both CPUs, state race and five analyzers. Original outputs and source captures are bound. The paired result is complete: UDP Save time fell 11.88% (p<.001), allocated bytes fell 21.34%, and allocation count/wire size were unchanged. Pointer Save/Load rose 2.75%/2.20% (p=.033/.017); six other timings were not significant. Executables grew less than 1%, and no process-RSS benefit is established. The observed wire.Save dispatch shape changed, but that is not a proven cause of the timing regressions. A narrow default-arm refinement at d837b98735 is now under separate correctness validation. The subsequent helper-dispatch paired experiment completed with UDP time down 15.86% and allocated bytes down 21.34%, unchanged allocation count/wire output, and no significant timing regression in eight controls. Its integration state.go/types.go differ from current master; the exact-current-package repeat is now independently reviewed. It improves UDP Save time 11.51% (p<.001) and allocated bytes 21.31%, with unchanged count/wire. Pointer Load improves 3.07% (p=.002), Map Load regresses 0.59% (p<.001), and six other timings are not significant. All 11 current-source correctness/analyzer targets passed. Root has now asked for contributor review of exact standalone 3b13f133c. Its per-arm wire size is 12,873 bytes and allocation count is 3,623, unchanged within that repeat; the earlier integration cohort used different absolute values.

The save-side legacy-byte capture experiment passed correctness but is rejected on its measured performance. In 12 paired comparisons (216 measured rows), UDP Save time rose 18.51%, allocated bytes rose 42.10% and allocation count rose 21.56%; wire size stayed 12,873 bytes. This compares modes in the same source containing the new plumbing, not the genuine unmodified parent. The separate checkpoint compatibility pilot passed six restore operations, but three operations per arm with the same reported executor-worker ID do not establish a timing effect or identical VM/CPU placement. The closed allocation profiles identify piece growth and per-struct capture storage as added costs. They are process-wide sampled estimates, not exact per-operation allocation accounting. No upstream proposal or speedup claim follows from this result.

Explicit type-owned registration corrects promoted snapshot dispatch on embedding parents. In e6dfccc3, both old snapshot leaves fail while their two legacy controls pass; all ten corrected owners pass, covering full state/wire on both CPUs, race and five analyzers. The original expected failed parent and zero cleanup/restoration status are retained. The earlier b8940bc2 nine-target pass lacked these embedding regressions and remains limited to its original fixture scope. No performance result follows from this correction.

evidence.label: Before/after registration regression and corrected owner scope

findings.text: The explicit typed-network records improved measured UDP queue Save by 10.70% (p<.001, twelve balanced pairs) and reduced allocated bytes by 8.61% and allocation count from 3,623 to 2,791, with identical 12,873-byte wire output. Eight ordinary control timings were not significant, while several Save controls allocated slightly more bytes. UDP initialization allocations rose from 98 to 349 per observed sequence and its executable grew 1.30%; those costs are outside the benchmark timer. All six separate full-kernel RestoreEmpty operations passed, without a statistical checkpoint timing claim. This is a source-specific prototype result; the earlier rejected representations remain recorded.

The ordinary StateSave/Sink consolidation passed all 19 original runtime/analyzer targets. Four mixed-graph streams and twelve UDP round trips are byte-identical across the baseline and candidate architectures/race variants. The parent f644e6d9 remains Failed because its result reader expected the wrong wire-test deadline and mishandled analyzer init-trace framing. Corrected saved replay closes the actual results without rerunning tests. The separate genuine-parent performance run b18345f5 is now closed and reported below.

evidence.label: Original compatibility run with saved-result correction

findings.text: The unified StateSave/Sink source 78ee4d756 improved UDP Save by 11.88% (p<.001, twelve balanced pairs), reduced allocated bytes by 8.72% and allocation count from 3,623 to 2,791, with identical 12,873-byte wire output. Map Save improved 1.53% (p=.002), while Map Load regressed 1.15% (p=.045); six other timing comparisons were not significant. Ordinary pointer/map/slice Save allocation costs match baseline. UDP initialization is unchanged at 51,496 B and 98 allocations per observed sequence, while the executable grows 1.15%. This is a separate one-worker cohort; no causal contribution is inferred by subtracting results from the previous optional-dispatch experiment.

Generated-record experiment 95eb0b3c compared exact 4e21551d7 with common-fixture parent c648363e8 in 12 balanced pairs on one pinned Linux AMD64 worker (52 actions, 216 measured rows). UDP Save fell from 526,951.5 to 466,043 ns (-11.56%, p<.001), bytes from 227,080.5 to 209,600 (-7.70%) and allocations from 3,623 to 2,790; wire size stayed 12,873 bytes. Pointer Save allocations rose from 5,043 to 6,068 (+1,025, +20.33%), with bytes +6.47%; map and slice Save each added one allocation. All eight control timing comparisons were nonsignificant. The UDP executable grew 9.71%, while per-sequence initialization allocations were unchanged. Eligibility correction 22cf74e12 passed all 19 compatibility targets; paired comparison 857951e7 is complete and recorded separately below. These measurements do not establish checkpoint-wide or RSS improvement.

The corrected 22cf74e12 cohort completed all 52 actions in 857951e7, with 216 measured rows and 12 balanced pairs against c648363e8. Owner-assessed UDP Save time is -10.07% (p<.001), bytes -8.05%, and allocation count 3,623→2,791; wire size remains 12,873 bytes. Pointer, map and slice Save byte/allocation counts now match baseline. Seven control timing comparisons are nonsignificant; ControlMessage Save is -7.73% (p=.002), -240 bytes and -10 allocations. UDP executable size is +5.58%, with 55,008 additional text bytes; observed initialization remains 51,496 bytes and 98 allocations per sequence. Independent numerical review is complete (d829e467e962). The separate kernel pilot 2576c8e3 passed all six restore operations on the same reported worker identifier, without proving the same VM or a checkpoint speedup. Do not subtract effects across the original and corrected cohorts.

The independent master extraction exposed a build dependency omitted by the earlier composition review. Generated tcpip emitters import pkg/state/wire, but master did not inherit the prototype’s handwritten-record dependency. Original ea0f9c0a is terminal Failed: eight checks passed and eleven were blocked during compilation. All 249 original files and 99 source bodies are retained. The shared records macro now supplies the generated dependency; both standalone and qualified corrections contain only that four-line change. All eleven blocked checks passed in 47fa61fb. The combined packet retains eight earlier passes and verifies four mixed-graph streams, sixteen primitive streams and twelve UDP round trips. The two unchanged master wire owners contain benchmarks but no Test cases, so they provide build coverage rather than wire assertions. The separate master paired measurement is now complete and reported below.

evidence.label: Original master extraction: missing generated dependency

findings.text: The independent master composition completed all 52 actions and 216 measured rows in twelve balanced pairs on one pinned worker. UDP Save was 475,377 versus 426,826.5 ns (-10.21%); allocated bytes fell from 288,497 to 270,401 (-6.27%) and allocations from 3,623 to 2,791, while wire size stayed 12,873 bytes. Pointer Save regressed 1.03% (p=.008) and Pointer Load 3.37% (p=.001). Slice Save improved 1.22% (p=.020) and ControlMessage Save 8.76%; four other timings were nonsignificant. Pointer/map/slice byte and allocation counts match baseline. Independent numerical review is complete (3e813f27dbfb). UDP executable size rises 5.85%, while observed initialization remains 51,496 bytes and 98 allocations per sequence. These measurements remain separate from the prior prototype cohorts. No checkpoint-wide or RSS improvement, readiness, or contributor approval follows from this result.

The concrete-header experiment passed nine compatibility owners and completed all 78 actions and 324 measured rows in twelve blocks. The owner rejects it as a refinement: against the generic representation, UDP Save is 0.77% faster but allocates 3.87% more bytes, while pointer Save is 0.94% slower and pointer Load has no significant change. Against master, the concrete-header arm still regresses pointer Save by 1.54% and Load by 2.13%. ELF inspection confirms the intended interface checks were removed; that did not eliminate the observed regressions. Independent numerical review is queued. This is a source-specific three-arm result, not a cross-cohort subtraction or a delivery proposal.

evidence.label: Completed three-arm header comparison: refinement rejected

findings.text: The separate native-region prototype reached actual before/after validation at ecbf9e3e3. Original parent 2e3f9019 is terminal Failed: both baseline state and UDP owners pass, including the new defined-pointer alias/nil/standalone and deferred-map witnesses. All thirteen candidate owners are compile-blocked by a stale val.obj reference in addrSetFunctions.Split after the owner rename. The 225-file/88-source archive is collected. That original attempt grants no candidate runtime or performance credit; the later source correction reuses its passed baseline results. This is separate from the held generic proposal receiver/import collision.

Native-region continuation a71bec71 passed all thirteen corrected owners at 91bdd8ef4. Saved comparison closes identical bytes/digests across the original baseline and corrected AMD64, ARM64 and race outputs, including named-pointer and deferred-map witnesses. The two passed original baseline owners are reused; the original Split compile failure remains preserved. The corrected archive contains 224 files and 88 source bodies, and owning input proof binds six fresh native binaries. Its later performance comparison is closed and rejected, as recorded separately below; no new contributor proposal is claimed.

Native-region representation 91bdd8ef4 is rejected on its own closed 12-pair comparison d14370c1: UDP Save is 3.34% slower, slice Save 29.58% slower and map Save 17.07% slower. Control-message Save is 1.92% slower; pointer Save and all four Load timing comparisons are nonsignificant. UDP adds 1,068 allocated bytes and four allocations per operation while retaining 12,873 wire bytes. The original 52 actions and 216 measured rows are collected. UDP executable size grows 1.45%; its observed initialization remains 51,496 B and 98 allocations per sequence. This is an incremental comparison with generic records at 9f6814106, not a new master comparison or a whole-checkpoint result. Overlapping process RSS observations establish no retained-memory benefit. Six bounded before/after CPU/allocation profiles are closed as 1733d8be, with 392 files and 106 source bodies retained.

The reference-array storage experiment at c2b1d942 passed fourteen compatibility owners and four-way byte/digest comparisons in 35a615dd. Its separate 12-pair comparison 5de5d3cf is now closed: slice Save time falls 27.20% (p<.001), allocated bytes fall 18.43%, and allocations fall from 1,067 to 43. All eight other timing comparisons, including UDP, are nonsignificant; this does not establish equivalence. Other allocation counts and wire sizes are unchanged. Both executable file sizes are unchanged, although each text section grows 1,440 bytes. Observed UDP initialization remains 51,496 B and 98 allocations per sequence. The 52 actions and 216 measured rows compare the generic-record baseline 4271fb2ca with the reference-array candidate on one reported remote worker, not fresh master or whole-checkpoint performance. The first RestoreEmpty pilot 702eb065 failed compilation in both arms before any tests: an older packetmmap caller expected a bool from the overlaid master packet endpoint's void API. Its 184 original files and zero-runtime result remain preserved. The matching-caller continuation 1c5f3b65 also failed compilation before any tests because another netstack caller depended on the overlaid networking API. Both failed attempts remain zero-runtime evidence. The coherent qualified-kernel pilot bac18fb7 subsequently completed all six restore operations; the two mixed-tree failures remain preserved. Independently, the master-based state/UDP compatibility run edbd6fc8 passed fourteen owners with four-way streams/digests and eight native binary joins. The separate genuine-master paired comparison c2ad6d98 is closed and reported below, including its UDP regression. These cohorts remain distinct from the measured generic-record baseline, and no checkpoint gain is claimed.

evidence.label: Original mixed-tree pilot: compile failure before tests

findings.text: The independent master repeat c2ad6d98 at 0ddbcf476 reports a significant UDP Save regression of 1.52% (p=.023). Slice Save improves 27.93% (p<.001), allocated bytes fall 18.43%, and allocations fall from 1,067 to 43. Map Load improves 1.27% (p=.017); six other timings are nonsignificant. Other allocation counts and reported wire sizes are unchanged. Independent numeric review verifies 52 original logs, 216 rows and twelve pairs. Both executables grow 4,096 bytes (about 0.08%); observed UDP initialization remains 51,496 B and 98 allocations per sequence. The coherent-kernel pilot bac18fb7 completed all six RestoreEmpty operations, establishing compatibility only. Equal reported worker IDs do not establish the same VM, and three operations per arm do not establish a checkpoint speedup. The original mixed-network pilots remain compile failures before tests. The one-file kind-dispatch refinement passed all eight affected compatibility owners in 301eb325, reusing the exact original baseline and unchanged wire owners. Six corrected runtime binaries bind the changed encoder source. The separate completed three-arm comparison 5b1e64cd is recorded with the reference-array proposal; these older results alone establish no refined performance benefit. These results do not transfer the prior generic-record gain to master.

The final reference-array refinement is retained after the balanced three-arm experiment 5b1e64cd: twelve blocks and all six source-order permutations twice, 78 actions and 324 measured rows. Against master, Slice Save improves 28.30% (p<.001), allocated bytes fall 18.43%, and allocations fall from 1,067 to 43. investigations.title: Scheduled tracker refresh reliability
investigations.summary:
The default-branch workflow now requests full refreshes every ten minutes. The unchanged collector uses 19 requests and 112 GraphQL points per sweep; six runs per hour fit the conservative 1,000-point workflow-token budget. The revised workflow passed all 29 JavaScript and 33 Python checks and published a live-verified snapshot. GitHub had not created runs for the first two revised slots by 05:10 UTC, so unattended scheduling reliability remains unverified. Active ownership now checks for ten-minute staleness and an existing queued or running refresh before using the same manual dispatch.

Before the correction, the active default-branch workflow requested runs at minutes 18 and 48, but the eight observed scheduled runs were created two to four hours apart. Their creation and start timestamps matched, which locates the observed gap before job execution. No disabled workflow, inactive repository, wrong default branch or inactive actor was found; the provider cause remains unknown. GitHub documents that scheduled events can be delayed or dropped. Manual refreshes do not establish a scheduler repair.

findings.text: At the 11 October schedule audit, the default-branch workflow was configured for minutes 18 and 48 of each UTC hour. The latest scheduled run observed by that audit was created at 01:01:30 UTC on 11 October and completed the 01:03:14 snapshot in status-only commit 560dd0edb. That newer automated snapshot was preserved before the curated update. Five earlier scheduled runs succeeded on 10 October, created at 01:18, 07:45, 13:59, 18:39 and 22:00 UTC. Successful execution is established, but the observed multi-hour gaps before event creation do not demonstrate regular 30-minute cadence. Their cause remains unexplained.

The configuration and run-history audit found no disabled workflow, wrong default branch, blocked job or queued run explaining the gap. The missing events occur before job execution, so there is no failed job log identifying their cause. No replacement scheduler or repeated re-registration has been introduced.

GitHub documents that scheduled jobs can be delayed or dropped. That is a service limitation, not proof of this gap’s cause. Manual publication through the existing collector is keeping verified snapshots visible while regular automatic cadence remains unproven.

The October 15 scheduled refresh collected successfully but lost a publication race to a metadata update. Workflow acffb2cb5 now recollects on the latest site revision after a confirmed concurrent update. The validation run reproduced that race and published on its second attempt; Pages deployed the new snapshot while preserving the README update. Authentication or transport failure against an unchanged remote head still fails the job.

The request-limit failure came from repeatedly fetching terminal source and import history. The corrected collector uses a complete open-PR inventory to discover reopening, confirms closures of previously active records, and refreshes known active imports even under terminal sources. Thirty Python regression cases run before snapshot collection in Actions. The successful live run used 20 requests and preserved 131 terminal-source observation clocks; historical terminal details do not acquire a fresh timestamp.

The enabled workflow on the actual default branch schedules minutes 18 and 48 each UTC hour. The 17 October audit found no newer scheduled event after the successful 00:31 run through 03:29 UTC, despite valid configuration and no queued or disabled job. A scheduled run subsequently resumed at 05:02:07 UTC and succeeded, producing the 05:02:58 full GitHub snapshot. That snapshot is preserved in the published site. The earlier missing events have no job log identifying their cause, which remains unknown; one successful resumed run does not establish regular 30-minute cadence. Event sweeps retain their separate observation clocks.

investigations.title: Runtime startup performance
investigations.summary:
The current integrated state proposal 3a38641f0 has a matched startup comparison against its prerequisite base. CLI medians are 2.380 versus 2.397 ms (p=.410), and StartupEmpty medians are 283.7 versus 265.8 ms (p=.198); neither establishes a timing difference or equivalence. State initialization remains 3,032 bytes and 13 allocations in both runsc and Sentry. Production file growth is 98,304 bytes for AMD64 runsc, 253,952 for AMD64 Sentry, 131,072 for ARM64 runsc and 262,144 for ARM64 Sentry. This source-specific comparison is separate from the earlier scalar and rewrite measurements below; samples are not pooled.

Earlier scalar-source record:

The scalar-store candidate 0fb39effd has verified matched CLI and StartupEmpty comparisons against original baseline 685d734a5: 6.104 to 6.113 ms (p=.887) and 479.1 to 476.5 ms (p=.551). Both are inconclusive, with unchanged pkg/state initialization allocations. The separate checkpoint/restore run failed and is under diagnosis. The earlier immediate-pair comparison against e0e088476 also found all ten package timing differences inconclusive; those samples are not pooled with the original-baseline startup comparisons. The candidate retains its verified code-size reduction, but remains 245,760 bytes larger per AMD64 binary and 196,608 bytes larger per ARM64 binary than the original implementation. It is not ready for contributor review.

Earlier source-specific startup evidence:

The earlier state rewrite at 91323cf62 completed matched Linux AMD64 CLI and sandbox startup comparisons: 5.868 to 6.054 ms (p=.143) and 251.116 to 254.198 ms (p=.932). Both are inconclusive. Each current AMD64 runsc/Sentry file grows by 2,351,104 bytes and each ARM64 file by 2,293,760 bytes; this is not measured RSS.

Fixed Linux AMD64 CLI comparisons for netip, the earlier state design, the owned-Value successor and the compiler-only change found no statistically significant timing difference. The compiler-only comparison also found no statistically significant sandbox-start difference (346.079 to 341.365 ms, p=.977, twelve batch means per version). It uses matched Go 1.26.3 sources. The owned-Value state CLI result remains 6.814 to 6.973 ms (p=.478), with production-file growth of about 4.01 MB on AMD64 and 3.74 MB on ARM64. The matched netip sandbox comparison also found no statistically significant difference: 288.4 to 296.1 ms (p=.590), with twelve batch means of eight starts per arm. It uses frozen Go 1.27.0 sources 6212e4f7b and 86ea1d1f3, not current upstream. Earlier state sandbox results concern their then-current source. These measurements do not establish equal startup cost or qualify the owned-Value successor for sandbox startup. The independent contributor-approved gofer initialization correction is published as #15859; its public checks and review remain under observation.

findings.text: The netip migration adds three binary-codec registrations and changes header initialization. Both comparison arms include the cheaper non-race registration from #15814. The fixed method measures 12 balanced pairs of 64 fresh runsc --version processes on one worker, with separate initialization traces and matching AMD64/ARM64 builds. CLI measurements do not substitute for sandbox startup.

All 1,536 timed CLI invocations completed. Twelve balanced batch means per arm give 8.398 ms before versus 8.034 ms after, with wide variation and no established timing effect. The AMD64 and ARM64 executable lengths are unchanged. Separate single-process initialization traces show 152 additional allocated bytes and seven additional allocations overall, including 104 bytes and six allocations in pkg/state. These traces are outside the timing samples.

The state rewrite’s separate CLI measurement gives 6.483 ms before and 6.816 ms after (p=.198, 12 paired batches), with no established timing effect. AMD64 and ARM64 executable lengths increase by 4,042,752 and 3,866,624 bytes. Separate initialization traces show +304 B and +6 allocations overall. The separate sandbox comparison is now complete and is recorded below.

The existing StartupEmpty benchmark completed 288 container starts in twelve balanced blocks on one Linux AMD64 worker. Median process means are 288.4 ms for the baseline, 296.1 ms for netip and 299.6 ms for the state rewrite. Neither difference is detected (p=.590 and .887). Source-built release inputs, actual child outputs and private-daemon cleanup are independently verified. The result measures this startup fixture and does not establish equivalence or cold-machine startup cost.

The gofer eagerly constructed cgo seccomp rules during package initialization, including for pure-Go binaries and precompiled-filter hits. The independent correction constructs a fresh rule set only when generating CgoEnabled rules. Existing config tests and analyzers pass on both architectures, with original-output and source-to-binary verification complete. A matched pure-Go AMD64 trace on the qualification branch removes 648 bytes and seven allocations; executable lengths are unchanged. This branch includes the separate musl clone rule, so those counts are not a standalone result. The check supplies no latency or plugin-runtime measurement. Contributor review of the standalone correction is now requested.

The owned-Value successor completed 1,540 processes in the fixed Linux AMD64 CLI protocol, with no statistically significant timing difference across twelve batch means per version: 6.814 to 6.973 ms, p=.478. Production file growth is 4,005,888 bytes on AMD64 and 3,735,552 bytes on ARM64. These are separate latency and size observations; the earlier sandbox comparison used a different state design. Independent source/native verification is complete. The separate package comparison is now complete with mixed results, including three Load regressions.

The matched compiler-only Go 1.26.3 comparison found no statistically significant startup difference. The existing 1,540-process CLI experiment has twelve batch means per version with medians of 5.543 and 5.801 ms (p=.347); its exact saved input rows were reused without more CLI sampling. The separate sandbox experiment completed 24 processes and 192 fresh starts in twelve balanced AB/BA blocks, with batch-mean medians of 346.079 and 341.365 ms (p=.977). Existing StartupEmpty times Spawn; shutdown and report handling are outside that interval. Source, release inputs, original process reports, order and arithmetic are verified. This is Linux AMD64 startup on the recorded workers, not an equivalence, cold-machine, plugin-runtime, CGO or ARM64-runtime result.

The retained netip sandbox experiment completed twelve batches of eight fresh starts per arm. Batch-mean medians are 288.4 ms for 6212e4f7b and 296.1 ms for 86ea1d1f3 (p=.590). Original processes, configuration, arithmetic and source/native inputs are independently verified. This frozen Go 1.27.0 comparison is inconclusive; it does not establish equivalence or current-upstream startup cost. No additional run was needed.

The matched current-source startup comparison is verified for 685d734a5 versus 91323cf62, including the split runsc/Sentry binaries and all eight release files. Linux AMD64 CLI medians are 5.868 to 6.054 ms (p=.143), from twelve batch means of 64 timed children per arm. StartupEmpty medians are 251.116 to 254.198 ms (p=.932), from twelve batch means of eight starts per arm. Neither comparison found a statistically significant timing difference; neither establishes equivalence. Each AMD64 runsc and Sentry production file grows by 2,351,104 bytes, and each ARM64 file by 2,293,760 bytes. The growth is code and Go metadata, not debug sections; it is not a measured RSS cost. Untimed state initialization adds 64 bytes and one allocation in each split binary. Whole-program initializer totals change by -96 bytes and no allocations for runsc, and +112 bytes and two allocations for Sentry. Both arms share #15648 and #15814; their benefits are not attributed to the rewrite.
